correctness.rationale: Exact block diagonalization of the weaving Gram form reduces optimal squared bounds to the norm of a cross-subspace compression. Center-of-arc geometry gives the upper bound \(\sin(\pi\theta)\); the half-line cross matrix is a shifted Hilbert matrix and an inverse-square-root finite trial vector has the matching logarithmic Rayleigh quotient with the exact Hilbert-matrix norm \(\pi\). Coercivity of the projected multiplier proves that every subcritical synthesis is onto, not merely a Riesz sequence. A Hardy function supplies a nonzero orthogonal vector above the critical phase; at the critical phase logarithmically divergent regularized Hardy vectors have uniformly bounded analysis energy. The direct proof treats all claimed real phases. The 250 numerical tests verify signs and normalizations but not infinite quantifiers.

value.rationale: Sharp condition estimates for every arbitrary binary switching pattern are an intrinsic and practically motivated quantitative question in woven Fourier bases. The exact optimal squared constants, one-sided worst-case design, and quadratic boundary condition-number blowup are a meaningful spectral classification not available from the generic qualitative Kadets criterion. This is neither a mere rephrasing of the threshold nor an arbitrary finite-parameter computation.
